question: Can body-only HTTP fingerprint observation (body hash as sole discriminating signal) maintain auth-state discrimination across production-like Keycloak middleware with non-deterministic infrastructure headers that add CDN, load-balancer, compression, and rate-limit noise?
hypothesis: Body-only fingerprint discrimination (M_BODY_ONLY_DISC) is invariant to non-deterministic infrastructure header noise, while full-vector fingerprint discrimination (M_FULL_VECTOR_DISC) degrades monotonically with noise intensity. This validates body-only as the robust architecture for production environments where CDN, load-balancer, and rate-limit middleware inject non-deterministic response headers.
falsifier: Body-only discrimination degrades below 0.8 on /userinfo at any noise level (breaks M_BODY_ONLY_INVARIANT), OR body-only discrimination degrades below 0.4 on /introspect at any noise level (breaks M_WEAK_BODY_INVARIANT), OR full-vector discrimination does NOT degrade with increasing noise on /userinfo (breaks M_NOISE_DEGRADATION), OR positive control fails (baseline body-only at noise=0 differs from parent EXP-RUNTIME-34439061845 by >0.05).
baselines: B-NO-NOISE-FULL-VECTOR: full-vector discrimination at noise=0 (no injected headers, pure Keycloak responses)
B-NO-NOISE-BODY-ONLY: body-only discrimination at noise=0 (baseline reference)
B-NO-NOISE-STATUS-ONLY: status-code-only discrimination at noise=0 (structural floor)
B-HIGH-NOISE-FULL-VECTOR: full-vector discrimination at noise=4 (8 injected headers)
B-HIGH-NOISE-BODY-ONLY: body-only discrimination at noise=4 (should equal B-NO-NOISE-BODY-ONLY)
positive_control: At noise=0, /userinfo body-only discrimination (M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE0) must equal or exceed 0.8 (parent observed 0.833; tolerance accounts for session timing). This confirms the measurement pipeline reproduces the parent result before noise injection.
null_control: At noise=0, /userinfo body-only discrimination (M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE0) must exceed 0.4 (floor: expired==invalid indistinguishable by body). This confirms the pipeline does not produce spurious noise.
measurement_validity: Keycloak 25.0 start-dev on localhost:18080 (Docker, same as parent experiments)
4 auth states: no_auth, valid_token, expired_token, invalid_token (same as parent)
Fingerprint algorithm: SHA-256(repr((status, tuple(sorted(filtered_headers.items())), body_sha256, redirect_chain))) — identical to parent EXP-RUNTIME-34439061845
Body-only fingerprint: SHA-256(repr((status, '', body_sha256, ''))) — status and body only, no headers
EXCLUDED_HEADERS: {date, server, x-request-id} — same as parent
Noise injection via Python reverse proxy on port 18081, forwarding to Keycloak on 18080
N=10 requests per auth state per noise level per endpoint (4 states x 10 reps x 4 noise levels x 2 endpoints = 320 total requests)
Random seed=44 for noise generation (deterministic across runs)
Jitter: 50-150ms uniform between requests (same as parent)
Noise levels defined as number of injected response headers: 0, 1, 2, 4
Proxy does NOT modify response body, status code, or auth-related headers (Cache-Control, WWW-Authenticate, Set-Cookie)
Proxy adds only infrastructure-irrelevant headers: X-Cache-Status, X-CDN-Request-Id, X-Edge-Location, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, X-Rate-Limit-Reset, X-Proxy-Upstream, Content-Encoding (identity), Vary
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE0 >= 0.8 (positive control), (2) M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE0 > 0.4 (null control), (3) M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE{1,2,4} all >= 0.7 on /userinfo (M_BODY_ONLY_INVARIANT), (4) M_BODY_ONLY_DISC_NOISE{1,2,4} all >= 0.3 on /introspect (M_WEAK_BODY_INVARIANT), (5) Spearman rho(M_FULL_VECTOR_DISC_NOISE{0,1,2,4}, noise_level) <= -0.5 on /userinfo (M_NOISE_DEGRADATION), (6) no pipeline errors — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for C-MEAS-VALID. If (3) fails: verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (body-only not invariant to header noise). If (5) fails: verdict = MIXED (full-vector does not degrade, body-only advantage is marginal). If (1) or (2) fails: verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: Body-only fingerprint discrimination is production-ready for auth-state detection under realistic infrastructure noise. SPIDER can safely use body-hash-only observation in production environments with CDN, load-balancer, compression, and rate-limit middleware. Product architecture should adopt body-only as the default fingerprint strategy, ignoring response headers entirely.
product_consequence_negative: If body-only discrimination degrades under header noise, the body-only architecture is not production-robust. Product must either (a) invest in noise-robust body normalization, (b) retain header-aware fingerprinting with infrastructure-specific calibration, or (c) accept reduced discrimination accuracy in production. This would materially change the product architecture recommendation from EXP-RUNTIME-34439061845.
estimated_cost: Low: Keycloak Docker (same as parent, ~2 min startup), Python reverse proxy (~100 lines), 320 HTTP requests total, no model calls, no browser automation. Estimated wall-clock: 15-20 minutes including Keycloak startup.
expected_information_gain: Medium-high: Directly tests the production-readiness claim from EXP-RUNTIME-34439061845. A positive result closes the infrastructure-robustness question for body-only architecture. A negative result identifies a new failure mode (header noise sensitivity) and redirects product architecture. The noise-sensitivity curve (4 levels) provides more information than a binary test.
